articles.headline: Barcelona to return to Olympic Stadium next season as Camp Nou costs rise to €2 billion
articles.description: Barcelona will return to the Olympic Stadium for several months next season after approving another €510 million ($585m) of financing to finish the Spotify Camp Nou redevelopment project.
articles.headlineJa: カンプ・ノウの費用が20億ユーロに急増、バルセロナは来季もオリンピック・スタジアムを使用へ
articles.descriptionJa: バルセロナはスポティファイ・カンプ・ノウの改修プロジェクトを完了させるため、さらに5億1000万ユーロ（約5億8500万ドル）の資金調達を承認したことを受け、来季も数ヶ月間にわたりオリンピック・スタジアムを使用することになった。
articles.body:
Barcelona will return to the Olympic Stadium for several months next season after approving another €510 million ($585m) of financing to finish the Spotify Camp Nou redevelopment project.

Barça moved back to Camp Nou last November after two years at the Olympic Stadium, but they must move out again ahead of the start of the 2027-28 season to allow the roof to be put on the redeveloped Camp Nou.

Speaking at the club's AGM, treasurer Ferran Olivé confirmed the plan is for Barça to finish the current campaign at Camp Nou before beginning next season at the Olympic Stadium.

The Spanish champions then plan to return to Camp Nou in January 2028, for the second half of the 2027-28 season.

The capacity at Camp Nou is currently capped at 62,000, with only two of the three tiers open, although Olivé says it will increase to 75,000 before the end of the current campaign as the third tier gradually opens.

By the time Barça return to Camp Nou in 2028, the capacity will have risen to 95,000, finally hitting 105,000 ahead of the 2028-29 season, when the stadium should be completely finished.

UEFA announced last week that Barça's iconic home will host the Champions League final for the first time in 30 years in 2029, so there is little margin for further setbacks.

The stadium revamp, which began in 2023, is running with severe delays. The date for the work to be completely finished has been continually pushed back, which has hit the club financially.

As a result, Barça members had to approve a €510m ($585m) financing package over the weekend to "cover the economic impact caused by delays in the execution of the project," pushing the total cost up to almost €2 billion ($2.3b).

- Barcelona's Andreas Christensen injures thigh, doubt for next Clásico

- Women's Champions League Power Rankings: Are Barcelona favorites again?

"The operation is structured in two components," Barça announced in a statement.

"The first consists of €300m ($344m) which will enable the completion of Camp Nou, a project whose scope has expanded significantly beyond the original plans through the addition of new facilities, services, and technological solutions.

"The second component consists of €210m ($241m) to be raised through two Media Notes issuances of €105m ($120m) each. The first was issued in July 2026, while the second is scheduled for October or November 2026.

"Both issuances have maturities of up to 10 years, carry fixed interest rates, and are secured against future audiovisual revenues generated from La Liga and UEFA competitions."

Barça are reliant on finishing the project to help drive the club's revenue in the coming years.

They predict income will rise significantly thanks to "additional stadium-related revenue, including ticketing, VIP hospitality, the museum and other associated activities with the team's return to Camp Nou."

articles.headline: Soccer's wildest warmup kits of 2026-27: The good, the bad and the ugly
articles.description: Forget home, away and third alternate jerseys -- the prematch warmup kit is where the real fun is to be had. Get a load of this season's best and worst.
articles.headlineJa: 2026-27シーズン サッカー界の最も斬新なウォーミングアップキット：最高、最悪、そして奇抜なデザイン
articles.descriptionJa: ホーム、アウェイ、サードユニフォームのことは忘れましょう。本当の楽しさは試合前のウォーミングアップキットにあります。今シーズンのベストとワーストをご覧ください。
articles.body:
With the 2026-27 season now underway across Europe's big leagues, we've had the chance to see teams limbering up in their new array of warmup apparel.

Predominantly worn by players while milling around on the pitch before kick-off, the designated "prematch" shirt has become a staple of the range in recent years. Many clubs put increasing amounts of effort and care into crafting said jerseys and even creating multiple variations or colorways that compliment their latest home and away kits.

Now that all of the big clubs have been in action for a few weeks, we've had the chance to peruse their respective prematch offerings and run a fashion-conscious eye over them -- whether they be good, bad, or indeed, irredeemably ugly.

- Premier League 2026-27 kits: Ranking every jersey released

- Bayern Munich's 2026-27 Oktoberfest kit is their wildest yet!

- Why this international break is longest ever (and that's a good thing)

THE GOOD

Barcelona

Barcelona have a lovely set of home and away variants for their prematch garb this season. The former is a rather appealing reworking of their famous Blaugrana club colours into a chic checkerboard design. Much like their Kobe Bryant collab "Mamba mentality" away kit, the alternate prematch jersey is a purple nebula design that comes with matching metallic logos and matte gold trim. Very Cyberpunk, much like Gavi's neon pink hair.

Manchester United

The red rose of Lancashire takes centre stage on Manchester United's warmup top this season, with multiple silhouetted graphics of the symbolic flower being picked out in red against a black backdrop. Possibly just one rose blooming around the club crest might have produced a  more streamlined effect, but it's a smart effort nevertheless.

Liverpool

Liverpool have used the very same "LFC" pattern found on their new 2026-27 away kit to add texture to the all-red home version of their new pre-match shirts. The motif is inspired by printed decoration found on vintage Anfield tickets stubs from the 1970s and 80s and really helps to elevate the design.

Real Madrid

Real Madrid have implemented the same rosy pink and bottle green colour combo across all of their home, away and third kits this campaign, with the prematch shirt sharing the same palette. The simple, smart retro design comes complete with raglan sleeves, a V-neck collar, Adidas trefoil logo and the club's initials ("RMCF") printed across the back of the shoulders.

Paris Saint-Germain

PSG's standard livery is melded in such a way as to create an eye-catching melange of neon purple hues thanks to the optical illusion created by the narrow pinstripes and the swirling gradients of red and blue in the background. There's also an oversized PSG crest slapped bang in the centre for good measure -- but still the design feels cool and dynamic rather than cluttered.

articles.headline: Doc Rivers joins NBC as analyst, says coaching career over
articles.description: Doc Rivers turned down an offer to become an NBA analyst for NBC after retiring as a player in 1996 because he couldn't promise then-NBC Sports chairman Dick Ebersol that he wouldn't become a coach.
